root_cause.text: The LoongArch BPF JIT failed to apply LoongArch ABI-required sign/zero extension to BPF kfunc call arguments before emitting a native function call, so arguments could be passed in the wrong width/sign state and trigger a kernel panic.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a special `if (insn->src_reg == BPF_PSEUDO_KFUNC_CALL)` block in `arch/loongarch/net/bpf_jit.c` that looks up the kfunc model and calls new `emit_abi_ext(ctx, reg, m->arg_size[i], sign)` for each argument; the commit message explicitly says “kfunc calls are native calls so they should follow LoongArch calling conventions” and “Sign extend its arguments properly to avoid kernel panic,” which shows the bug was missing ABI-correct argument extension in the JIT path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix kfunc JIT call preparation by validating the function model and ABI-extending arguments before emitting the call.
intent_record.what: The JIT build_insn() path now checks whether the BPF call is a BPF_PSEUDO_KFUNC_CALL, and if so it looks up the kfunc's BTF function model with bpf_jit_find_kfunc_model(); on failure it returns -EINVAL, and on success it iterates over all declared arguments, maps each argument register, derives whether the argument is signed from m->arg_flags, and emits ABI extension handling via emit_abi_ext() for each argument before emitting the call address and jirl instruction.
intent_record.how: At runtime, kfunc calls are now prepared according to the callee's actual BTF-described argument sizes and signedness, ensuring arguments are properly extended to the ABI width before the call is made. This prevents incorrect register passing for kfunc invocations and rejects calls when the kfunc model cannot be resolved.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add ABI-aware register extension handling in the JIT to preserve correct signed and unsigned value semantics.
intent_record.what: A new static inline helper function `emit_abi_ext()` was added. It takes a JIT context, a register, a value size, and a sign flag, and emits size-appropriate LoongArch extension instructions: it returns immediately for unsigned 1- or 2-byte values, emits `extwb` for 1 byte, `extwh` for 2 bytes, `addiw reg, reg, 0` for 4 bytes, does nothing for 8 bytes, and warns on invalid sizes. A comment describing ABI-related extension requirements was also added above the function.
intent_record.how: The new helper centralizes ABI-mandated register extension behavior for values already in a register. It ensures signed narrow values are properly sign-extended and that unsigned char/short values remain zero-extended as required by the ABI, preventing incorrect high bits from being propagated into later JIT-generated code.

    LoongArch: BPF: Adjust the parameter of emit_jirl()
    
    The branch instructions beq, bne, blt, bge, bltu, bgeu and jirl belong
    to the format reg2i16, but the sequence of oprand is different for the
    instruction jirl. So adjust the parameter order of emit_jirl() to make
    it more readable correspond with the Instruction Set Architecture manual.
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in the BPF kfunc/call path. In the `/* function call */ case BPF_JMP | BPF_CALL:` block, the code only does `move_addr(ctx, t1, func_addr);` and then `emit_insn(ctx, jirl, LOONGARCH_GPR_RA, t1, 0);` followed by `move_reg(ctx, regmap[BPF_REG_0], LOONGARCH_GPR_A0);`. There is no ABI handling of kfunc call arguments here, and no sign/zero extension of call parameters before the native call. The root cause described is exactly that LoongArch BPF JIT failed to apply LoongArch ABI-required sign/zero extension to BPF kfunc call arguments before emitting a native function call. This snippet shows the call emission path but lacks any argument-extension fix, so the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet present.

    LoongArch: Add BPF JIT support
    
    BPF programs are normally handled by a BPF interpreter, add BPF JIT
    support for LoongArch to allow the kernel to generate native code when
    a program is loaded into the kernel. This will significantly speed-up
    processing of BPF programs.
    
    Co-developed-by: Youling Tang <tangyouling@loongson.cn>
    Signe
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is the initial LoongArch BPF JIT implementation, and it does not contain any kfunc-call argument handling logic at all. The only native function-call path shown is the BPF helper/call case: `case BPF_JMP | BPF_CALL:` followed by `move_imm(ctx, t1, func_addr, is32); emit_insn(ctx, jirl, t1, LOONGARCH_GPR_RA, 0);`. There is no code here that marshals BPF kfunc arguments, and no sign/zero-extension step for call arguments before a native call.
